propositions: A parent removed in Jira is never cleared in the local parent_id field because the snapshot omits the parent key when it is None, making a de-parented issue indistinguishable from one never parented.

The inbound differ refuses to emit parent_id=None to avoid accidentally clearing a locally-set parent when the parent key cannot be resolved, conflating two distinct cases: observed-absent and unresolvable.

The managed_refs gate alone cannot establish that Jira ever had the parent—it only proves the ref was set locally—so clearing based on managed status alone destroys parent edges that were never pushed to the peer.

A clear must fire only on positive evidence that the peer once carried the parent; without persisted peer-state history, a degraded read (truncated page, REST failure, {}  degradation) cannot be distinguished from an actual deletion.

The same-pass outbound write suppression cannot fire for parent because the outbound parent emit gate is disjoint from the peer's accept constraints, leaving the residual window (degraded outbound pass) as the normal case rather than an edge case.
